messages.subject: geom_boxplot vs boxplot
parts:
this is my reproducible example

site.teq<-structure(list(site = structure(c(1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 1L, 3L,
4L,
1L, 5L, 5L, 1L, 5L, 1L, 1L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 1L, 1L, 3L, 4L, 1L, 5L,
1L, 3L, 4L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 1L, 1L, 5L, 1L, 1L, 5L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L,
5L), .Label = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"), class = "factor"),
iteq.1989 = c(3.37, 4.59, 2.32, 4.79, 89.58, 0.9, 20.49,
1.21, 0.72, 0.96, 0.3, 0.89, 0.73, 1.29, 0.47, 0.03, 21.37,
31.28, 42.25, 5.51, 32.79, 96.62, 30.17, 36.1, 1.49, 61.04,
0.53, 1, 2.12, 0.7, 6.25, 0.44, 0.33, 0.58, 16.53, 22.7,
18.24, 626.66, 42.71, 59.87)), .Names = c("site", "iteq.1989"
), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -40L))

and this is my code

# ggplot boxplot
ggplot(site.teq, aes(factor(site),iteq.1989))+
geom_boxplot(fill="red", outlier.size=2, outlier.colour="black")+
scale_x_discrete("site")+
scale_y_log10(name=expression("[ "*"fg "*m^-3*" ]"),
limits=c(10^-2,10^3), breaks=c(10^-2,10^-1,10^0,10^1,10^2,10^3),
formatter="scientific")+
theme_bw(base_size = 10)

# boxplot
boxplot(iteq.1989 ~ site, data=site.teq,
col="red",
xlab="site", ylab=expression("[ "*"fg "*m^-3*" ]"),
ylim = c(10^-2,10^3), yaxt="n", log="y", yaxs="r")

axis(side=2, at=c(10^-2,10^-1,10^0,10^1,10^2,10^3))

now my problem is the following:
by looking at the two charts, the one produced with ggplot through
"geom_boxplot" and the corrispondent generated with the usual function
"boxplot", it seems that results are based on a different definition
of outliers...is that somehow plossible?
...surely, I'm missing something, any help for that?

sorry for such a trivial question but I'm moving around my first steps
in R and ggplot....

thanks

> "boxplot", it seems that results are based on a different definition
> of outliers...is that somehow plossible?

I suspect the difference is that ggplot2 is computing the boxplots on
the log scaled data, and base graphics is computing on the raw data
and then scaling the outputs.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: geom_boxplot vs boxplot
parts:
Hi Max,
scales are applied before stats and coords are applied afterwards.

P <- ggplot(site.teq, aes(factor(site), iteq.1989)) +
geom_boxplot(fill="red")
#boxplot of log transformed data
P + scale_y_log10()
# boxplot of raw data displayed on log axis
P + coord_trans(ytrans = 'log10')
